walkthroughIntro.inOneLine: Separate the explanation from its predictions, plan a fair test, and decide what the observed results do and do not support.

lenses.name: Propose competing explanations
lenses.instruction: Write one tentative explanation and an alternative. State what is already observed and which part is still an assumption.

lenses.name: Make a discriminating prediction
lenses.instruction: Predict an observable difference if your explanation is useful. Name the measure, expected direction and a result that would weaken the explanation. Compare the alternative prediction.

lenses.name: Design the comparison
lenses.instruction: Describe the comparison, assignment or sampling approach, measurement window and decision rule chosen before seeing results. Identify confounders and limits. Use a safe, proportionate test; do not claim a sample is adequate without justification.

lenses.name: Interpret results or record the gap
lenses.instruction: If results exist, record the raw counts or observations, compare them with the prediction and describe uncertainty. If the test has not run, write "Results not yet collected" and identify what to collect; do not invent an outcome.

- **Room:** 1F2051
- **Date:** 2026-09-20
- **Participants:** 2 participants (anonymous)
- **Time:** 0 min (budget: 31 min)

## Decision
Run a two-week randomized comparison of current versus clearer title, holding price, schedule and layout fixed. The title explanation predicts a higher completed-signup rate; a flat or lower rate weakens it, while an unsuitable schedule remains an alternative. Predeclare a one-percentage-point practical threshold and assess uncertainty before adoption; wide uncertainty is inconclusive. Results not yet collected: 36 signups from 1200 earlier visitors is baseline context only. Collect group counts, assignments and errors, and verify the analysis plan before launch.
